name: Boston Massacre
kicker: Soldiers fire on a Boston crowd, March 1770 · A spark for the Revolution
briefing: On a cold March night in 1770, with snow on the ground, an angry crowd in Boston threw snowballs, ice, and insults at British soldiers outside the Custom House. The soldiers fired into the crowd, and five colonists died, including Crispus Attucks. Paul Revere’s engraving of the scene spread outrage across the colonies, but John Adams defended the soldiers in court, and most of them were found not guilty.
answerHtml: Boston Massacre (accept Incident on King Street; do not accept “Boston Tea Party”)

qb.tip: Search QBReader for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked) to see how real tossups clue it.

tossups.p: Less than two weeks before this event, an 11-year-old boy named Christopher Seider [“SY-der”] was killed when a customs worker, Ebenezer Richardson, fired a gun from his house into a crowd of protesters. Samuel Adams helped organize a huge funeral for the boy, which raised anger against British officials in the same city.
tossups.r: In this event, British soldiers fired into a crowd on King Street. For 10 points, name this 1770 event in which five colonists died.

tossups.p: Three days before this event, a fight broke out at John Gray’s ropewalk, a rope-making yard, after a worker there insulted a soldier who was looking for a part-time job. Many off-duty British soldiers took such jobs for low pay, which angered local workers.
tossups.r: Days later, soldiers fired into a crowd on King Street. For 10 points, name this 1770 event in which Crispus Attucks died.

tossups.p: This event began when a wigmaker’s apprentice named Edward Garrick insulted a British officer, and a sentry, Private Hugh White, struck the boy with his musket. A crowd soon surrounded White outside the Custom House, and Captain Thomas Preston marched seven soldiers to help him.
tossups.r: Those soldiers fired into the crowd on King Street. For 10 points, name this March 1770 event in which five colonists died.

tossups.p: On the same day as this event, Lord North asked Parliament to repeal most of the Townshend duties, keeping only the tax on tea. News crossed the Atlantic so slowly that colonists did not hear about that repeal until weeks after this event.
tossups.r: In this event, soldiers under Captain Thomas Preston fired on a crowd. For 10 points, name this 1770 event in which Crispus Attucks was killed.

tossups.p: Henry Pelham accused a silversmith of copying his drawing of this event without permission. That silversmith’s hand-colored print of this event showed soldiers firing in a neat line on their captain’s order, an image that spread anger across the colonies.
tossups.r: That silversmith, Paul Revere, titled his print _The Bloody Massacre_. For 10 points, name this 1770 event in which British soldiers killed five colonists.

tossups.p: Patrick Carr, who died more than a week after this event, told his doctor that he forgave the soldier who shot him and that he believed the soldiers had been provoked. That deathbed statement helped the defense at the trials that followed this event.
tossups.r: John Adams helped defend the British soldiers. For 10 points, name this 1770 event on King Street in which Crispus Attucks died.

tossups.p: The day after this event, a committee led by Samuel Adams demanded that acting governor Thomas Hutchinson remove British troops from the city. Hutchinson agreed to move both regiments to Castle William, a fort on an island in the harbor.
tossups.r: In this event, soldiers had fired into a crowd outside the Custom House. For 10 points, name this 1770 event that Paul Revere showed in a famous engraving.

tossups.p: After this event, a captain was tried separately from his men and found not guilty, because witnesses could not agree on whether he had ever given the order to fire. In a later trial, six of his soldiers were found not guilty and two were convicted of manslaughter.
tossups.r: That captain was Thomas Preston, and John Adams was the soldiers’ lawyer. For 10 points, name this 1770 event in which British soldiers fired on a crowd in Boston.

tossups.p: Robert Treat Paine, a future signer of the Declaration of Independence, helped prosecute the eight soldiers accused in this event. Josiah Quincy Jr. joined their defense even though his own brother, Samuel Quincy, was one of the prosecutors.
tossups.r: Their most famous defense lawyer, John Adams, later became the second president. For 10 points, name this 1770 event in which soldiers fired on a crowd on King Street.

tossups.p: Hugh Montgomery and Matthew Kilroy were the only soldiers convicted after this event, and both were found guilty of manslaughter rather than murder. They avoided a harsher punishment by claiming an old legal privilege called “benefit of clergy,” which could spare a first offender from the death penalty.
tossups.r: Their lawyer, John Adams, later became president. For 10 points, name this 1770 event in which Crispus Attucks died.

tossups.p: During the trials that followed this event, a lawyer reminded the jury that “facts are stubborn things.” He argued that the soldiers had fired in self-defense after people in the crowd threw snowballs, ice, and clubs at them.
tossups.r: That lawyer, John Adams, defended the soldiers even though he supported the colonists’ cause. For 10 points, name this March 5, 1770, event in Boston.

tossups.p: From 1771 to 1783, Bostonians held a public speech every March 5 to remember this event, and Joseph Warren gave that speech in 1772 and again in 1775. John Hancock gave the 1774 speech, before July 4 took over as the town’s main patriotic holiday.
tossups.r: This event happened on King Street in 1770. For 10 points, name this clash in which British soldiers killed five colonists.

tossups.p: In 1858, abolitionists in Boston began holding a yearly celebration honoring the first person killed in this event, and in 1888 a monument to all of its victims was unveiled on Boston Common. That first victim was a sailor of African and Native American descent.
tossups.r: That victim was Crispus Attucks. For 10 points, name this 1770 event in which British soldiers fired into a crowd.

tossups.p: A circle of cobblestones near the Old State House marks the spot of this event, on what was then called King Street. A lone sentry was guarding the Custom House, where customs money was kept, when an angry crowd gathered there.
tossups.r: Five colonists died there in March 1770. For 10 points, name this event that helped turn colonists against Britain.

tossups.p: The soldiers involved in this event belonged to the 29th Regiment, one of the units sent to the city in 1768 to protect customs officials collecting the Townshend duties. Colonists mocked those soldiers as “lobsterbacks” because of their red coats.
tossups.r: Paul Revere made a famous engraving of this event. For 10 points, name this 1770 event in which five colonists were killed on King Street.

clues.t: On March 5, 1770, British soldiers fired into a crowd of colonists in Boston
Five colonists died; Crispus Attucks, a sailor of African and Native American descent, is remembered as the first to die
Paul Revere’s engraving of it spread anger across the colonies
John Adams defended the soldiers in court; most were found not guilty
Happened on King Street (later renamed State Street) outside the Custom House
Captain Thomas Preston led the soldiers; he was tried separately and found not guilty
The crowd threw snowballs, ice, and insults at the soldiers
British troops had been in the city since 1768 to protect customs officials collecting the Townshend duties
Of the eight soldiers tried, six were found not guilty and two were convicted of manslaughter
Samuel Adams used it to stir up anger and pressed to get the troops out of town
Less than two weeks earlier, customs worker Ebenezer Richardson killed 11-year-old Christopher Seider; Samuel Adams helped organize the funeral
A fight at John Gray’s ropewalk (March 2, 1770) started over soldiers taking part-time jobs
It began when apprentice Edward Garrick insulted an officer and the sentry, Private Hugh White, struck him
The same day, Lord North asked Parliament to repeal most Townshend duties, keeping the tax on tea
Revere copied Henry Pelham’s drawing; his print was titled _The Bloody Massacre_
Victim Patrick Carr told his doctor he forgave the soldier who shot him and thought the soldiers were provoked
Acting governor Thomas Hutchinson moved the troops to Castle William in the harbor
John Adams: “Facts are stubborn things”; he argued the soldiers fired in self-defense
Robert Treat Paine and Samuel Quincy prosecuted; Josiah Quincy Jr. helped John Adams defend the soldiers
Hugh Montgomery and Matthew Kilroy, convicted of manslaughter, escaped the death penalty by claiming “benefit of clergy”
Yearly March 5 speeches (1771–1783) by speakers such as Joseph Warren and John Hancock
Abolitionists began a yearly celebration honoring Crispus Attucks in 1858; a monument went up on Boston Common in 1888
A circle of cobblestones near the Old State House marks the spot
The soldiers were from the 29th Regiment; colonists mocked redcoats as “lobsterbacks”

trap.title: Massacre or Tea Party?
trap.body: Boston had two famous showdowns before the Revolution: the Boston Massacre (March 5, 1770), when soldiers fired into a crowd, and the Boston Tea Party (December 16, 1773), when the Sons of Liberty dumped tea into the harbor. Both involve Samuel Adams and British taxes, so buzzing early on “Boston” clues can go wrong. Some tossups instead want a person from this event: Crispus Attucks or John Adams.
trap.fix: Massacre clues: King Street, the Custom House, Captain Thomas Preston, snowballs, and Revere’s engraving. Tea Party clues: Griffin’s Wharf, the ship _Dartmouth_, disguises as Mohawk Indians, and the Tea Act. Listen for “this event” versus “this man” or “this lawyer.”
trap.line: Real answer line: Boston Massacre (accept Incident on King Street)
